first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent me this with a one-line summary: a calm, well-sourced seasonal guide, written for couples deciding between Europe and the islands. The first screen, "March is a shoulder month for a wedding abroad, so the question is which kind of shoulder you want," is sensible and not eager, which I respect. But nothing in it tells me this team has handled 300 guests, closed a property or worked with a security detail. I skimmed the headings and the closing section. I did not read the weather figures.

journey.quote: March is a shoulder month for a wedding abroad, so the question is which kind of shoulder you want.
journey.reaction: Measured and not salesy. Good tone. It doesn't promise anything it can't deliver.

journey.section: How we chose these ten March destinations
journey.quote: Each place here is one we plan and write about, and the list is unranked.
journey.reaction: Fine, but 'plan and write about' says nothing about the scale of what they plan there. I want to know what's possible, not that they've written a guide.

journey.quote: gives a March minimum temperature of 10.4°C, a mean of 13.4°C and a maximum of 15.8°C.
journey.reaction: Honest, but this is detail my assistant would skip. Every entry has this level of weather data and it reads like a reference page rather than a planner's view.

journey.quote: Is there an indoor or covered space that holds the whole guest list if it rains?
journey.reaction: This is the right kind of question for us. With a guest list our size, the covered option is the first thing that fails.

journey.quote: Is the villa open for weddings in March, and which rooms are heated for dinner and dancing?
journey.reaction: Practical, but the question I'd actually ask first is whether the whole villa can be ours for the days we need. It isn't anywhere in the post.

journey.quote: What happens to the wedding, and to guests' rooms, if a cyclone closes the airport that week?
journey.reaction: Good. That's the kind of contingency thinking I expect, and it's put plainly without fear-mongering.

journey.quote: Tell guests honestly what to pack: a jacket for Europe, an umbrella for the islands.
journey.reaction: This is written for a different client. Our guests are coming from Dubai, London and Sydney, and packing tips feel like over-explaining.

journey.section: Plan your March wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One advisor start to finish is reassuring for discretion. But 'quotes in AUD' tells me the page is built for Australian couples on a set budget, and nothing here says the team works at our scale.

journey.section: Plan your March wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Tell us your date, your guest list and anyone who needs extra care getting there,
journey.reaction: Thoughtful about elderly family, which matters to us. But there's no word on privacy, so my assistant has no reason to raise discretion or security in the first message.

unanswered_questions: Has this team delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests at any of these destinations?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a whole property, and do they have experience doing so?
How do they handle privacy: NDAs, no-photography policies for staff and suppliers, keeping the wedding off social media?
Will they coordinate with our own security team alongside the venue's?
Is there a private or referral channel to enquire, rather than a public form?
Do they have experience with family customs and catering needs for a Gulf family, and how do they handle them?

turn_offs_found.quote: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD,
turn_offs_found.why: Reads as aimed at an Australian couple comparing prices. Not offensive, but it places me in the standard client group I'm worried about.

turn_offs_found.quote: Tell guests honestly what to pack: a jacket for Europe, an umbrella for the islands.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. A planner at my level would just handle guest communications for us.

cta_reaction.quote: When your shortlist is ready to become dates and venues, begin with [Wedded Concierge]
cta_reaction.why: I only enquire through a private channel or a referral. Nothing here suggests discretion or large-scale experience, so my assistant would note the brand and move on unless someone we trust recommended it.

top_3_changes: Add exclusive use to a venue question. Old: "- Is the villa open for weddings in March, and which rooms are heated for dinner and dancing?" New: "- Is the villa open for weddings in March, can the whole property be taken for exclusive use, and which rooms are heated for dinner and dancing?"

Invite privacy needs in the closing ask. Old: "Tell us your date, your guest list and anyone who needs extra care getting there," New: "Tell us your date, your guest list, any privacy or security needs, and anyone who needs extra care getting there,"

Add a discretion question to the guest planning section. Old: "Ask each venue how older or less mobile guests move around in wet weather." New: "Ask each venue how older or less mobile guests move around in wet weather, and how it keeps the day private from other guests and the public."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, Dubai, assistant reads first, private channel only)
No invented brand facts; missing information listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored

Suggested edits are exact old/new strings that add no prices, statistics, weather figures, rankings, 'best', 'free', vendor or venue names, fees, on-the-ground staff, transfers, room blocks, availability, holiday dates or legal claims
Scores are 1 to 5 and top_3_changes has no more than 3 items

open_questions.question: This is a mass-audience seasonal guide and the UHNW persona is provisional (weight 0.20). Should a low likelihood_to_enquire here count against the post, or only drive the small privacy and exclusive-use edits?

assumptions: Arrival context was not specified; assumed Layla's assistant found the post through search and forwarded it with a summary.
